caching.note: Models before GPT-5.6: automatic prefix caching, implicit only, with no cache-write charge. OpenAI publishes no minimum cacheable length for them (it varies with request settings) and no breakpoint interval length. Lifetime depends on retention: in_memory keeps entries around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour; 24h typically around 30 minutes, up to 24 hours. Which retention Copilot uses isn't documented.

assumptions.text: OpenAI documents no tools/system/messages render order, only that stable content should come first. The simulation assumes tools → system → messages, so the tools and system rules are inferred.
Which cache lifetime Copilot requests for GPT-5.6 and later (the 30-minute default or 12 hours) isn't documented. The simulation assumes the 30-minute default.

For GPT-5.6 and later, 30 minutes is a minimum lifetime, and a read extends coverage to at least 30 minutes after it. The simulation treats an entry as expired 30 minutes after its last read or write, though it may survive longer.

For GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.4 nano, Copilot's retention is probably in_memory: GitHub has a zero data retention agreement with OpenAI, and OpenAI defaults organizations with Zero Data Retention to in_memory on models that support both values. No doc states this for Copilot, or which values these two models support.
Changing reasoning effort can change model-side reasoning instructions, and so the prefix. OpenAI doesn't say from which point, so the rule is unknown.
Reasoning tokens are billed as output tokens.

Copilot bills GitHub's tiers (rule register owner decision 3): GPT-5.6 Luna's long-context tier starts above 200K input tokens on GitHub, though OpenAI's pricing page shows 272K for all models; the other tiered models start above 272K. The long-context output prices are GitHub's, which differ from OpenAI's own page data (owner decision 4, open).
GitHub's thresholds ('≤ 200K', '≤ 272K') are read as 200,000 and 272,000 input tokens; GitHub doesn't define K.
GitHub doesn't say which tokens count toward a tier threshold or whether the long-context tier prices the whole request. The simulation prices the whole request by its total input tokens.

sources.quote: GitHub maintains a zero data retention agreement with OpenAI.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching
sources.quote: Prompt caching is enabled by default for supported OpenAI models.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (implicit breakpoint, GPT-5.6 and later)
sources.quote: OpenAI places a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (minimum length)
sources.quote: The minimum cacheable prompt length is 1,024 tokens for GPT-5.6 and later and varies by request settings for earlier models.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (minimum length, earlier models)
sources.quote: For models before GPT-5.6, the minimum cacheable input length varies with request settings, including tools, images, output schemas, reasoning effort, and verbosity.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (implicit breakpoints, earlier models)
sources.quote: Spaced at regular, model-dependent intervals.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (supported retention values)
sources.quote: Supported retention values | "30m" (default), or "12h" in the Responses API | "24h" only | "in_memory" or "24h" *

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (cache lifetime, GPT-5.6 and later)
sources.quote: set `prompt_cache_options.ttl` to choose the minimum cache lifetime.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (refresh on read, GPT-5.6 and later)
sources.quote: A 30-minute read refreshes coverage to at least 30 minutes after that read. If it uses an entry with valid 12-hour coverage, it preserves the later of the existing expiry and 30 minutes after the read. It does not restart a 12-hour clock or incur another write charge.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (cache-write charge, GPT-5.6 and later)
sources.quote: cache writes cost 1.25× the standard, uncached input-token rate for the default 30-minute lifetime.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (in_memory retention)
sources.quote: in_memory: Entries typically remain active for around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (24h retention)
sources.quote: 24h: Extended retention typically keeps entries available for around 30 minutes and can retain them for up to 24 hours.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (default retention with Zero Data Retention)
sources.quote: Organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled default to in_memory.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (prefix match)
sources.quote: Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (tool changes)
sources.quote: Changes tool names, descriptions, schemas, ordering, or tool-specific instructions.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (prompt structure)
sources.quote: Put stable developer instructions and shared reference material first.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (model changes)
sources.quote: A different model can use different weights and caching behavior.

sources.title: OpenAI: Prompt caching (reasoning effort changes)
sources.quote: Can change model-side reasoning instructions.

sources.title: OpenAI: API pricing (long-context toggle)
sources.quote: Long: >272K input tokens

sources.title: OpenAI: Reasoning models
sources.quote: While reasoning tokens are not visible via the API, they still occupy space in the model’s context window and are billed as output tokens.
